subject.title: feature: system event priority/bypass-queue mode for reliable in-session alerts

question: Should OpenClaw add a privileged high-priority system-event path, and should it bypass heartbeat/session lanes or be a separate typed operator notification surface?
rationale: Current code intentionally skips active command and session lanes to preserve streaming/session ordering; bypassing that changes trusted prompt injection, abuse controls, and session integrity.

options.title: Design explicit priority alert contract
options.body: Define auth scope, sanitization, rate limits, ordering, transcript behavior, and tests before adding a narrow priority system-event path.

options.title: Use typed notification surface
options.body: Make immediate TUI/operator alerts the canonical urgent path while keeping prompt-visible system events heartbeat-mediated.

options.title: Keep best-effort semantics
options.body: Document that prompt-visible system events can be delayed under saturated lanes and rely on external channels or pre-failure triggers for outage alerts.

recommendation.title: Design explicit priority alert contract
recommendation.body: Define auth scope, sanitization, rate limits, ordering, transcript behavior, and tests before adding a narrow priority system-event path.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans Gateway wake behavior, CLI contract, notification policy, and security/session-state semantics where the current history points most strongly to steipete.
